summary: Integrate React Doctor (https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor) into the Namias portfolio marketing site and drive the codebase to a perfect 100/100 health score. The deliverable is a fully-wired integration: devDep install, baseline capture, per-category fixes, GitHub Action regression blocking, agent skill documentation, and a locked-in score threshold enforced on every PR.
narrative: The portfolio today ships a lot of React across 50+ components: hero, projects, certifications, gallery, blog, floating hub, booking modal, resume modal, chat panel, command palette, motion wrappers, theme provider, lenis scroll root, and more. Without an enforced code-quality gate, the surface area has drifted into the anti-patterns React Doctor was built to catch: unmemoized callbacks, missing useMemo on derived values, exhaustive-deps violations, unkeyed list children, prop drilling, inline event handlers, forgotten effect cleanups, and stale closures. This slice installs the tool, captures the baseline, walks the codebase rule by rule, and ends with a CI check that blocks any PR that drops the score. The agent skill 'run-react-doctor' teaches future contributors (and agents) how to read the report, which rules are unavoidable, and how to fix each finding without breaking visual or functional parity.
principles: Score over opinion - the score is the contract; fixes must move it up, not be aesthetic.
One rule at a time, one commit at a time - the report is granular, the fixes should be too.
No behavior change without a screenshot - every fix keeps visual + functional parity; the playwright baseline must pass.
Ignore generated and test code, not hand-written code - .react-doctor.json scopes exclusions to the right paths.
CI is the source of truth - the local script is for iteration, the GitHub Action is the gate.
Document the why, not just the what - the agent skill explains each rule, the rationale, and the canonical fix pattern.

personas.label: PP Namias (owner)
goals: Keep the marketing site React-quality best-in-class without manual lint roulette.
Ship features without each new component regressing the score.
Trust the CI check to block regressions before they land.
painPointsToday: No automated gate on React anti-patterns.
exhaustive-deps and react-hooks rules buried in eslint output, easy to skip.
No score history to compare against.

personas.label: OpenCode / future coding agent
goals: Read a single SKILL.md and know how to run, read, and fix React Doctor findings.
Be able to read the report and know which rules to silence (none, in our config) and which to fix (everything else).
Have a copy-pasteable fix template per rule category.
painPointsToday: No list of allowed-vs-disallowed rule tweaks.

personas.label: Hiring manager / reviewer
goals: See the React Doctor badge on the README + a green CI check on PRs.
Click into the per-PR comment and see the score delta and findings.
Trust that the score is real (not padded by exclusions of hand-written code).
painPointsToday: No visible quality signal in the repo.
Hard to tell if the codebase is React-best-practice at a glance.

primary: React Doctor score is exactly 100/100 on src/** (excludes test files and generated code).
Every PR runs the react-doctor GitHub Action; the action blocks merges when the score drops.
react-doctor is installed as a devDep and runs in < 10 seconds on the current codebase.
secondary: All 12 react-doctor rule categories report 0 findings on the marketing source tree.
An agent skill 'run-react-doctor' exists in .agents/skills/ with copy-pasteable fix recipes per rule.
A baseline report (FINDINGS.md) is committed at EPIC-1 close for historical comparison.
demo: Local: `npm run doctor` prints the score, lists zero findings, exits 0.
CI: a draft PR with a deliberate exhaustive-deps violation is blocked with a clear comment.
Skill: an agent can read .agents/skills/run-react-doctor/SKILL.md and fix a finding without further help.

antiPatterns: Silencing rules wholesale via config to game the score - the score is the contract.
Bypassing the GitHub Action via admin merge - the action must stay green.
Refactoring for the score in a way that breaks the visual baseline - playwright must pass.
Touching test files for the score - test files are out of scope (.react-doctor.json excludes src/__tests__/**).
Touching generated code (next-env.d.ts, .next/**, studio/dist/**) - out of scope.

ruleCatalog.label: Giant components
ruleCatalog.fix: Extract sub-components; aim for < 200 lines per component.

ruleCatalog.label: Exhaustive dependencies
ruleCatalog.fix: Add the missing dep; if intentional, wrap the value in useMemo or move it inside the effect.

ruleCatalog.label: Unmemoized callbacks
ruleCatalog.fix: Wrap with useCallback; pass stable deps.

ruleCatalog.label: Unkeyed list children
ruleCatalog.fix: Use a stable id (slug, _key, uuid) as the key; never the array index for re-orderable lists.

ruleCatalog.label: Inline event handlers in hot paths
ruleCatalog.fix: Extract to a named handler, or accept the cost if the list is small and the prop is the children.

ruleCatalog.label: Direct state mutation
ruleCatalog.fix: Always return a new object/array from the setter; never push/splice on state.

ruleCatalog.label: Missing effect cleanup
ruleCatalog.fix: Return a cleanup from useEffect that aborts, clears timers, removes listeners.

ruleCatalog.label: Conditional hooks
ruleCatalog.fix: Hooks must run in the same order every render; guard above the hook, not inside.

ruleCatalog.label: Stale closure capture
ruleCatalog.fix: Use a ref for the latest value, or include the value in the deps array.

ruleCatalog.label: Async without cleanup
ruleCatalog.fix: AbortController, cancelled flag, or a mounted ref.

ruleCatalog.label: Prop drilling
ruleCatalog.fix: Context, composition, or a co-located state owner; never > 2 levels.

ruleCatalog.label: Forgotten useMemo
ruleCatalog.fix: Memoize any derived value used in render or as a dep of a memoized child.
